short.titel: HIS BIGGEST MISTAKE: BUFFETT'S TEXTILE TRAP
short.text:
Buffett's oral deal shrank in writing. His angry reaction became his biggest investment mistake.

In 1962, his fund bought Berkshire shares at $7.50, expecting a profitable tender offer.

In 1964, he offered his shares back at $11.50. The manager orally agreed.

So what arrived in writing? Only $11.375. Buffett admitted that made him angry.

Instead, he bought more stock at an even higher price to take control.

That shrunken deal left him controlling a declining textile business. He said it denied him about $200 billion.
